idea-plugin.name: Repotory
idea-plugin.description:
The local-first memory layer for AI coding agents.
Ask your Repotory knowledge base a question from inside the IDE and read the answer with its sources, without leaving the editor.
Repotory keeps what your coding agents learn — why a decision was made, what gotcha you hit, what to do next — in a local, searchable store. This plugin is the console for it:
• A conversation, not a result list: you ask a question, the turn joins the feed, and the turns stay there. The newest two stay open; older ones fold into one row and open on click, so "what did I just ask" is always one click away. • Three knowledge faces, one keystroke apart: Ask answers with prose and a folded "Sources" list, Notes brings up your notes and todos, Pages brings up the approved knowledge pages. A note or a page opens IN PLACE, inside the turn that produced it. • Locked to your project by default: the chip next to the modes shows which project the panel is scoped to, and clicking it puts the panel back to cross-project. Ask and Pages really filter server-side; Notes cannot (the tool has no project parameter), so the panel filters the hits itself and tells you how many it dropped. • Full-text search (FTS5) over every note and todo you ever captured, ranked exactly as the Repotory desktop app ranks it — the plugin reimplements no ranking, no snippet extraction, no gating. • One-click jump: "Open in Repotory" deep-links the item into the Repotory web app. • Note maintenance without leaving the IDE: edit a note's title, kind, tags and 项目 (project), add a new note under the same 项目, or let the AI tidy a note into a restructured proposal — sections, an index, and a mermaid flowchart when the content is really a process. The proposal opens in the editor for your review; nothing is saved until you save it. • Works out of the box: the tool window checks the channel when it opens and shows the result as a status pill. If nothing answers, it starts the local repotory-server you already have — nothing is downloaded or built, and a service you started yourself is never touched.
The plugin is a thin client: its data goes over MCP to repotory-mcp, which opens the same local database the desktop app uses, and the two things that still speak HTTP talk to the loopback-only Repotory service. Everything stays on your machine — there is nothing to authenticate and nothing that leaves it. One build covers the whole IntelliJ family (IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand and the rest), on IntelliJ 2024.2 or newer, independently of your project's JDK.
